claims.text: Additive manufacturing of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 will enhance its oxidation resistance relative to casting and wrought processing.
The initial comparison material is Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 produced by casting or wrought processing.
Additive manufacturing is the proposed processing intervention for the alloy.
Gas-turbine, power-plant, and aerospace applications expose the alloy to relevant high-temperature environments.
Nanoprecipitates form during additive manufacturing of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Additive manufacturing promotes a unique microstructure in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The additive-manufacturing-induced microstructure enhances the alloy's oxidation resistance.
Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 will have a lower oxidation rate than cast and wrought counterparts.
Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 will perform better in high-temperature applications than cast and wrought counterparts.
The proposed comparison is limited to Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 and is not asserted to apply to other compositions.
